# Executive Summary

In 2026 I spent 350 hours of Google Summer of Code on [rdlocal](https://github.com/eliocamp/rdlocal) (formerly rhelpi18n, ISC grant 2023-2). You install a small translation module, set your language, and R's help pages show up translated. After the summer it handles dynamic help and package updates. It all works, but every translation is still typed by hand, and the help for `base` alone is about 1 million characters.

So I opened a Sprint issue pitching a bring-your-own-key machine translator. Paola Corrales, who had translated one module file, wanted the draft but not the per-user part, and she was right.

That became the design for **babelrd**: a companion package that will let a translation team machine-draft one shared rdlocal module per package and language, check that every page still renders, and then review the draft in Weblate or any PO editor. The MVP is `draft()` and `check()` with DeepL.

I'm asking for **$5,600** (140 hours at $40/h), December 2026 to June 2027, in four milestones ordered so partial funding still leaves a working tool.
